survey: A DJ controller with headphones, seen from the front and above at about 35°. The controller is a rounded rectangular box. Its top face tilts away from the viewer and you can see the thick front side band. It stands on short cylindrical feet, with the front-left foot clearly visible and the front-right foot partly hidden behind the headphones. On the top face are two platters, one on each side. Their outlines fit true ellipses with width ratios of about 0.64 on the left and 0.59 on the right, both with the short axis near vertical, which matches the tilt of the top face and changes gradually across it. A raised mixer section sits in the centre with two slots and green faders, and three round knobs stand at the back edge. Rows of coloured pads run along the front edge. The pad rows run parallel to the front edge of the controller (red edges near 7°), and the pad tops are drawn foreshortened like the top face. The side edges of the body lean inward toward the back (blue edges near 122° on the left and the matching edge on the right), so the box narrows consistently toward the back. The headphones stand upright on the floor in front of the controller's front-right corner. Both ear cups rest on their rims on the floor. The left cup shows its inner cushion turned toward the front-left, and the right cup shows its outer face turned toward the front-right. The headband arches above them and leans close to the controller's front edge. Their placement, size and floor contact fit the same raised viewpoint and the same floor as the controller.
